# Freeport-Mc Mo Ran (FCX) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 024 | Published 2020-06-21 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-6-21/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/024.json)

Summer caution alongside a copper investment thesis.

The Freeport volume expansion and subsequent copper-price recovery have clear operating support. Summer caution was less successful: equities, copper shares and breakevens rose while the dollar weakened. The exploration and electrification reasoning was useful; decade-long commodity superiority remains unresolved. The claim-count headcount and broad dismissal of further mandated shutdowns need correction.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 024-C01

**Fatality and containment estimates improved**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Evidence needed |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Pandemic |
| Source blocks | 14, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Thesis family | covid-fatality-containment |

Population death share is not infection fatality risk; age mix, reporting lags and hospital capacity matter. The comparison to experts is not operationalized. Country policy comparisons require adjustment for epidemic timing, testing and voluntary behavior.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** Compare age-standardized excess mortality and infection estimates with dated forecasts; avoid causal inference from country anecdotes.

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

### 024-C02

| Field | Assessment |

England imposed another national stay-home requirement in November 2020. One country cannot establish a global majority, but it decisively refutes treating major developed economies as having moved beyond enforced shutdowns. The broader most-governments count is not quantified.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: remainder of pandemic

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [New national restrictions](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/prime-minister-announces-new-national-restrictions) | UK Government | 2020-10-31 | Verified in the audit

England required staying home from November 5, 2020 except specified reasons, contradicting the expectation that enforced lockdowns were largely finished outside China.

### 024-C04

**Claims represent twenty-nine million people**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US unemployment |
| Source blocks | 29, 30, 34 |
| Thesis family | ui-claims-persons-confusion |

The article converts benefit-claim totals into a headcount. GAO later documented that weeks claimed did not reliably count distinct people because of processing backlogs. This does not deny severe labor distress, but invalidates the literal denominator.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [COVID-19 oversight report](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-21-265/index.html) | GAO | 2021-01-28 | Verified in the audit

GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

Personal income fell 4.2% in May after revised 10.8% growth in April. Declining recovery payments explained much of the decrease, partly offset by unemployment benefits. Spending rose 8.2%.

Reserves are electronic central-bank settlement money. Capital is a separate resource that absorbs loan-default losses; both liquidity and capital constraints apply to banks.

March 2020 global dollar funding pressures increased as wholesale funding contracted and hedging/credit-line demand rose. Swap-funded auctions helped foreign banks meet commitments and build liquid assets without selling dollar assets.

Weekly total assets rose from $4.183 trillion on February 12, 2020 to $4.242 trillion March 4 and $6.368 trillion April 15. A brief late-February decline preceded the surge.

American-style exercise is the holder's decision before expiration. At expiration, exercise-by-exception thresholds and contrary instructions apply; going in the money does not itself compel early assignment.
